who.value: buyer who won several lots in a Live show (and the seller on the other side)

stage.value: returns — after delivery, a return/refund request is open

job.value: Check where their return/refund request stands and which lots it covers

arrivedFrom.value: Order details of a live-show order, tapping into the return/refund

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The top card 'Reviewing your request — Your seller will respond with a resolution within 24 hours' says at once what the screen is for.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The status card leads, but the only filled button is 'Cancel request' at the very bottom, so the loudest action is the one that undoes the job.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'View details', 'View 2 more', 'View order details', 'Copy' and 'Cancel request' each say what they do.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: 'Lot #2', 'Near mint', 'Buyer Protection' and 'Return item, full refund' are terms a live-show buyer already knows.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: The buyer is only asked whether to cancel; nothing needs information they don't have.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Long lot lists collapse behind 'View 2 more' / 'View 4 more' and per-lot detail sits behind 'View details'.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: The 'Cancelled' and 'Received as described' lot sections share a page titled 'Return/refund details' with lots that aren't part of the request.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Lot rows carry the meaning through labels and prices; the only prose is the two-line status card.
